clue.text: Almost succeed — need this fixing

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop just short, dropping the final letter of the phrase for succeed

parts.note: to succeed is to do well

explanation.surface: Someone nearly managing a job finds it needs a repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the last L from DO WELL (succeed), leaving the five letters; 'need this' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden peg used as a fixing to join pieces of timber.

clue.text: Bomb takes an aimless line — design flaw

parts.note: a doodle is an aimless scribbled line
a bug is a flaw in a design, especially in software

explanation.surface: A bomb is drawn with a squiggle, revealing a defect in its plans.
explanation.walkthrough: A doodlebug was the British wartime name for the V-1 flying bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the wartime nickname for the German V-1 flying weapon.

clue.text: Grab some sound sleep

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for sleep is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: rest means sleep

explanation.surface: Snatch some deep, untroubled sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective for deep sleep; it is the signal to go by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to seize or wrench away by force.

clue.text: Not much enthusiasm for old exam

parts.note: little means not much
go means energy or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A lack of zeal for an old test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Little-go was the old first examination for a Cambridge degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Little-go was the nickname of the preliminary examination formerly taken at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Social worker confined inside becomes chippy

indicators.note: inside places the word for confined within the word for the social worker

parts.note: a carer is someone who looks after people, a social worker of sorts
pent, as in pent-up, means confined

explanation.surface: A care worker shut indoors grows irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' looks like the adjective meaning touchy; in British slang it is also a noun for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is informal British slang for a joiner, someone who works with wood.

clue.text: Fuel that's a drug on the market

explanation.surface: A fuel that is sold as a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is the fuel left after coal is heated; it is also slang for cocaine.

clue.text: Squander opportunity for practice

explanation.surface: Wasting a chance to rehearse.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through money is to waste it; a run-through is a rehearsal.

clue.text: Sergeant perhaps comes in before second performance

indicators.note: comes in means the soldier goes inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A sergeant enters ahead of the next show.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an extra performance demanded by the audience.

clue.text: Torn strap repaired in carriage

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so the letters of torn strap are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken strap is mended in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means conveyance, the carrying of goods or people.

clue.text: Businessman game at first for a dance

indicators.note: at first puts the game's letters ahead of the businessman's

parts.note: RU is rugby union
an MBA, Master of Business Administration, stands for a businessman

explanation.surface: An executive's game comes before a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: It's no secret a range of knowledge can be surpassed

parts.note: something overt is open, not secret
taken as written
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Knowledge that is openly shared can be outstripped.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overtaken is to be passed by someone going faster.

clue.text: Seduce church member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A parishioner is lured astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a church member, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to win them over, to beguile or entice them.

clue.text: Just now a student in the Fens

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
Ely is the cathedral city in the Fens of East Anglia, so in the Fens is at Ely

explanation.surface: A student has recently arrived in the flat East Anglian marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in the Fens, the low marshy country of eastern England; 'in the Fens' gives AT ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately means recently, a short while ago.

clue.text: Attractive quality daily is finished by mother

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A newspaper's appeal is rounded off by Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like a newspaper; a daily is also a British cleaning woman, a CHAR. 'finished by' just puts MA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, a compelling attractiveness.

clue.text: Two words for Goldwyn? No way

explanation.surface: The film mogul famous for mangled phrases rejects an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Goldwyn, the Hollywood producer, is credited with the line 'in two words: im-possible'.
explanation.definitionFit: No way means it cannot happen, so the answer is a flat refusal; Goldwyn reputedly split it in two.

clue.text: Game to put money on? Humbug!

parts.note: to back a horse is to put money on it
gammon is old slang for nonsense or humbug

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a game they could bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Cad in Havana gives one a lift

explanation.surface: A rogue in Cuba gives someone a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban heel is a moderately high heel on a shoe, which raises the wearer; a heel is also a cad, here a Cuban one.

clue.text: The round of housework

parts.note: the first half of housework, house, is abbreviated HO
the second half, work, is op, short for opus

explanation.surface: A circuit of household chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, a ring or round shape.

clue.text: Old bald-head doesn't finish tablet — it has a pungent smell

indicators.note: doesn't finish tells us to cut the last letter from the word for tablet

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
garlic is a strongly smelling bulb

explanation.surface: An old bald man fails to swallow a whole tablet, which smells strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilgarlic is an archaic word for a bald man, from a peeled head of garlic.

clue.text: Not very skilful in prose

explanation.surface: A clumsy writer of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Unversed means inexperienced or unskilled; writing in prose is literally not in verse.

clue.text: Take guidance from swimmer

explanation.surface: Follow the advice of a swimming coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by something is to be guided by it; a goby is a small sea fish.

clue.text: Since birth, sympathetic about onset of teething

indicators.note: about means the word for sympathetic goes round the other letter

parts.note: congenial means agreeable or sympathetic

indicators.note: onset of picks out the opening letter of teething

explanation.surface: A baby has been friendly from birth, despite starting to cut teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' gives T from teething, which 'about' places inside CONGENIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A congenital condition is one present from birth.

clue.text: Ratio of reflection from forged round blade

indicators.note: forged means shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: The gleam off a newly forged sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' signals the anagram; 'from' is only a link. Albedo is a term from astronomy and climate science.
explanation.definitionFit: Albedo is the proportion of incident light a surface reflects.

clue.text: Stupid, but don't care so much

explanation.surface: A fool, perhaps, but one who worries less.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless means thoughtless or stupid; to mind less is to care less.

clue.text: Mate in correspondence game

explanation.surface: Checkmate delivered in a postal chess game.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a partner who corresponds, an equal; it is also a sporting contest.

clue.text: A crime that's toppled old kingdom

indicators.note: toppled means knocked over, so the letters of a crime are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An offence that brought down an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of England, in the Midlands.

clue.text: Empty net

explanation.surface: An empty goal net.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear is to empty; to clear a sum is to net it as profit.

clue.text: 'Ladies only' sign?

parts.note: ladies only means nought males: O for zero
the excluded males are men

explanation.surface: A notice on a door for women only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies only' means no men: O (nothing) then MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of things to come.

clue.text: People here near London

explanation.surface: Folk who live in the home counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as THE SE, the South East: the region of England surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: These people are the ones present; split in two it is the region round the capital.

clue.text: Great shock in war correspondent's telegram?

explanation.surface: A stunning wire from a reporter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a stunning surprise; a war reporter's wire might literally announce a bomb and a shell.

clue.text: Welcome to think of old autumn night

parts.note: hallo is a greeting of welcome
ween is an archaic verb meaning to think or suppose

explanation.surface: A greeting to a bygone autumn evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is 31 October, the eve of All Saints' Day.

clue.text: Yorick would rhyme to order

explanation.surface: A poet looks for a rhyme for Hamlet's jester.
explanation.definitionFit: The word matches Yorick in sound; it also names one of the classical orders of architecture.
